name: Event Organization Portal - SIA Project 21 22
description:
Information Systems - academic year 21/22
Course Project
Version 1.0.1 - 20/12/2021
Consider the following scenario:

A startup intends to develop a web portal that can help people who intend to organize an event, bringing together in a single website the information concerning the guests and the various services necessary for the event itself to take place.

The platform to be developed envisages the presence of providers and guests, in addition to the organizer.

At registration, providers supply, in addition to their credentials, their personal data and the data of the company they manage (VAT number, company address, accepted payment methods).

The provider, once registered, will be able to enter the services offered by their company, each belonging to a category (catering, hairdresser, florist etc.), each of which will be associated with a virtual showcase in which the provider can upload demonstration photos, together with the corresponding prices and the hours corresponding to the particular service shown by the showcase (e.g. Hairdresser's blow-dry service has as hours 10:00-12:00 from Tuesday to Thursday, Haircut + shampoo service with hours 8:00-12:00 + 15:00-18:00 from Tuesday to Saturday).

The event organizer, identified by their tax code, at registration, in addition to choosing their credentials, will provide their personal data, residence data and their IBAN for the possible payment of the services.

The organizer, through the portal, will be able to create the event, choosing the type of event (wedding, graduation, concert…) to organize, the date, the place where it will be held and the budget planned for the organization of the event. When creating the event the organizer will be able to choose from a pre-existing list the types of service for which they are interested in receiving help (for example catering, flowers, taxi service etc.).

The organizer will also be able to add the guests to the portal, entering the corresponding data, specifying, in addition to the personal data, the email with which the guest will be identified (and which they will use to log in) and the category to which the guest belongs (relative, friend, colleague etc.).

For each guest added, the system will generate an invitation code that will be sent by email to the specified address; this code will be used by the guest as a password to access the portal.

The organizer will also have available a blog associated with their event in which the organizer or the guests can write information about the event, post photos or videos and leave their thoughts by creating new posts or commenting on the existing ones.

The organizer, once the event has been created, will be able to view, for each service chosen when creating the event, the showcases of the providers that supply the chosen type of service and to arrange an appointment compatible with the hours observed by that service, specifying the details and any special requests. The provider, through their interface, will be able to view the various appointment requests and will have to approve them. The approved requests are displayed directly in a calendar on the site associated with the event, where the organizer will be able to consult the appointments for the agreed services.

After the meeting between the provider and the organizer (in which they agree on the details of the service), the provider calculates the quotation and proceeds to upload the amount on the portal, associating it with the completed appointment.

Once the upload has taken place the organizer can choose whether to accept or reject the quotation; if it is accepted, the total amount is subtracted from the remaining budget. By accepting the amount, the organizer chooses the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance or full amount) and the payment method (online or on site). If the payment takes place on site the provider will proceed to confirm the amount paid through the portal (in the case of payment in several instalments the provider confirms the amount of each instalment received).

At any time the organizer will be able to consult the history of the contracts (with the related status and cost) and the budget balance for the entire event.
highLevelGoals: The Event Organizer aims to efficiently create, configure, and manage all aspects of an event, including type, date, location, budget, and required service categories, through a centralized web portal.

The Event Organizer seeks to easily add and manage guest information, including personal details and categories, and to facilitate the secure invitation of guests to their event via unique access codes.

The Event Organizer desires to discover and book suitable services for their event by browsing provider showcases, viewing service details, and arranging appointments that align with their event schedule and requirements.

The Event Organizer aims to maintain clear visibility into their event budget, track all service quotations, payment statuses, and contract histories to ensure financial control and informed decision-making.

The Event Organizer wishes to foster communication and engagement among guests and themselves through an event-specific blog, allowing for information sharing, photo/video uploads, and interactive discussions.
The Provider aims to effectively showcase their company's services, including detailed descriptions, demonstration photos, pricing, and availability, to attract potential Event Organizers.

The Provider seeks to efficiently manage appointment requests from Event Organizers, approve bookings, generate accurate quotations, and facilitate the payment confirmation process for services rendered.
The Provider desires a secure platform to manage their company credentials, personal data, and service-related information, ensuring accuracy and privacy.
The Guest aims to easily access relevant event details and participate in event-related discussions and content sharing through the event's blog.
lowLevelGoals: The Event Organizer can initiate the creation of a new event by providing a name and initial details through the web portal.
The Event Organizer can select and set the specific type of event (e.g., wedding, corporate, birthday) from a predefined list.
The Event Organizer can specify the start and end dates and times for the event using a calendar interface.
The Event Organizer can input and save the physical address or venue details for the event.
The Event Organizer can set and adjust the overall budget for the event, categorizing expenses as needed.
The Event Organizer can select the required service categories (e.g., catering, photography, entertainment) for the event.
The Event Organizer can register a new account by providing their tax code, personal data, residence, and IBAN.
The Event Organizer can input individual guest details (name, email, category) one by one into the system.
The Event Organizer can assign guests to specific categories (e.g., VIP, family, friends) for organizational purposes.
The system can automatically generate a unique, secure access code for each invited guest.
The Event Organizer can send an invitation email containing event details and the unique access code to selected guests.
The Event Organizer can view a list of available service providers, filtered by service category or other criteria.
The Event Organizer can access a detailed profile page for each service provider, including descriptions, photos, and reviews.
The Event Organizer can propose and confirm an appointment time with a service provider through an integrated calendar.
The Event Organizer can view a dashboard displaying the current event budget, allocated funds, and remaining balance.
The Event Organizer can view a list of all requested and received service quotations, including their status (pending, accepted, rejected).
The Event Organizer can accept a service quotation, choosing the payment mode (instalments, deposit + balance, or full amount) and payment method (online or on-site).
The Event Organizer can check the payment status for each booked service (e.g., pending, paid, overdue).
The Event Organizer can retrieve and review past contracts and agreements with service providers.
The Event Organizer can view approved service appointments displayed on an event-associated calendar.
The Event Organizer can compose and publish new blog posts on the event-specific blog.
The Event Organizer can upload images to be included in blog posts or a dedicated event gallery.
The Event Organizer can upload video files to be embedded in blog posts or an event video gallery.
The Event Organizer can view and reply to comments made by guests on blog posts.
The Provider can create and customize their company's service showcase page, including a company profile and branding.
The Provider can input detailed descriptions for each service offered, highlighting features and benefits.
The Provider can upload high-quality photos to visually demonstrate their services.
The Provider can define and update pricing structures for their services, including packages and hourly rates.
The Provider can manage and update their service availability calendar, blocking out unavailable dates or times.
The Provider can register a new account by providing their VAT number, company address, and accepted payment methods.
The Provider receives notifications for new appointment requests from Event Organizers.
The Provider can review and approve or decline appointment requests from Event Organizers.
The Provider can create and send a detailed quotation for requested services to an Event Organizer after a meeting.
The Provider can mark each instalment payment as received and confirmed for services rendered.
The Provider can securely update their company's login credentials and profile information.
The Provider can view and edit their personal contact information and other relevant data.
The Provider can modify details of their listed services, such as descriptions, pricing, and categories.
The Guest can view the event's name, date, time, and location after logging in with their unique access code.
The Guest can browse and read all published blog posts on the event's dedicated blog.
The Guest can view photos uploaded by the Event Organizer or other guests to the event gallery.
The Guest can write and submit comments on individual blog posts.
The Guest can compose and publish new blog posts on the event-specific blog.
The Guest can upload images to be included in blog posts or a dedicated event gallery.
The Guest can upload video files to be embedded in blog posts or an event video gallery.
